skos:definition: The lexical expression used by humans for identification purposes of geologic material
proposed_definition_concise: A name used to identify or refer to a geological material or specimen.
proposed_definition_technical: A lexical label, of any form and from any source, applied to a geological material, specimen, or specimen part to identify or describe it; the root name type from which all other name types in this vocabulary are specialized.
proposed_definition_plain: Any word or phrase people use to name a rock, mineral, meteorite, or other geological material.
proposed_usageNote: Use only when no narrower name type applies or when the origin and status of the name are unknown; prefer the most specific applicable type.
proposed_scopeNote: Includes names of minerals, rocks, meteorites, gems, and other geological materials, whether formal, informal, historical, or curatorial. Excludes names of places, geological units (e.g., formations), people, and biological taxa.
review_comment: Top concept. Original definition is sound; proposed wording makes the concept's role as the root name type explicit.

skos:definition: A name assigned by an authoritative body based on a defined set of unambiguous criteria and belonging to a formal nomenclature
proposed_definition_concise: A name assigned under a formal nomenclature by a recognized authority according to defined criteria.
proposed_definition_technical: A name established within a formal nomenclature by a body recognized as having authority over names in that domain, and assigned according to published, unambiguous criteria, such that its application can be verified against that authority's register or classification.
proposed_definition_plain: A name that an official expert body has set up and controls, following its own published rules.
proposed_usageNote: Apply to names traceable to a specific authority and nomenclature (e.g., IMA-CNMNC for minerals, the Meteoritical Society for meteorites, the IUGS Subcommission on the Systematics of Igneous Rocks for igneous rocks). Record the authority and, where possible, the version or date of the source consulted.
proposed_scopeNote: Encompasses names from formal classifications at any rank, officially registered names of individual entities (such as meteorite names), and solid-solution series names. Excludes informal, trade, varietal, historical, and curatorial names, which fall under Alternate Name or Object Name.
review_comment: altLabels 'Formal Name' and 'Official Name' duplicate the prefLabels of two separate concepts (Formal Name has an identical definition; Official Name is a narrower concept). Remove these altLabels, and either deprecate Formal Name or adopt the distinction proposed on that row.

skos:definition: A name derived from an authoritative classification system at any rank
proposed_definition_concise: An authoritative name that places a material in a category at a defined rank within a formal classification system.
proposed_definition_technical: An authoritative name designating a category at a defined rank (e.g., class, clan, supergroup, group, species) within a hierarchical classification system published by a recognized authority, and thereby assigning the specimen to that category.
proposed_definition_plain: The official name of the category a material belongs to in a scientific classification, at any level (for example, a group or a species).
proposed_usageNote: Where the rank is known, prefer the narrower Group or Species type. Record the classification system (and edition) from which the name is taken.
proposed_scopeNote: Covers names at any rank of formal mineral, rock, and meteorite classifications. Does not cover names of individual meteorites, which identify a single fall or find rather than a category (see Official Name).
review_comment: altLabel 'Species' collides with the prefLabel of the narrower concept Species; remove it. The prefLabel 'Classification' names a system rather than a name type; consider 'Classification Name'.

skos:definition: A group name based on a shared crystal structure and composition of chemically similar elements
proposed_definition_concise: A group name for minerals that share the same or essentially the same crystal structure and are composed of chemically similar elements.
proposed_definition_technical: A group name, as defined under IMA-CNMNC group nomenclature (Mills et al., 2009), for two or more mineral species that have the same or essentially the same crystal structure and are composed of chemically similar elements; such groups may be subdivided into subgroups or combined into supergroups.
proposed_definition_plain: The name of a family of minerals built on the same crystal structure with similar chemistry, such as the olivine group.
vann:usageNote: Recommended is the use of Fleischer's Glossary.
proposed_usageNote: Take group names from the current IMA-CNMNC list of mineral groups or from the latest edition of Fleischer's Glossary of Mineral Species, and record the source and edition used. Apply only where membership rests on shared structure and chemistry.
proposed_scopeNote: Includes IMA-recognized mineral groups, subgroups, and supergroups defined on structural and chemical grounds. Excludes groupings based solely on chemistry (e.g., chemical classes such as carbonates), physical properties, or commercial use.
review_comment: Original definition is near-identical to that of its broader concept Group, so the two cannot be told apart. Proposed text separates them: Group = any group-rank category in an authoritative classification; Structural Group = structure-and-chemistry group per IMA-CNMNC.

skos:definition: Name of the solid solution series to which a specimen belongs.
proposed_definition_concise: A name for a solid-solution series between two or more end-member mineral species.
proposed_definition_technical: A name designating a continuous or partial solid-solution series in which two or more end-member mineral species of the same structure type are linked by substitution at one or more crystallographic sites.
proposed_definition_plain: The name for a family of minerals whose chemistry grades smoothly from one pure end member to another, such as plagioclase (albite to anorthite).
proposed_usageNote: Use when a specimen's composition is known to fall within a series but has not been resolved to a species. Where the species has been determined, record the species name (type Species) instead of, or in addition to, the series name.
proposed_scopeNote: Covers solid-solution series between end-member species. Series names generally do not denote mineral species in current IMA-CNMNC nomenclature. Do not use 'series' as a synonym for 'group'.
review_comment: Placed under Authoritative Name, yet many series names in common use (e.g., plagioclase) are not IMA-approved species. Consider moving under Classification, or allowing informal series names under Alternate Name.

skos:definition: A mineral name that has received formal approval by the International Mineralogical Association (IMA)
proposed_definition_concise: A mineral name recognized as valid by the IMA Commission on New Minerals, Nomenclature and Classification (CNMNC).
proposed_definition_technical: A mineral species name recognized as valid by the International Mineralogical Association through its Commission on New Minerals, Nomenclature and Classification (CNMNC), whether by formal approval of a new-mineral proposal, by approval of a renaming or redefinition, or by grandfathered status for species described before 1959, and listed as valid in the current IMA List of Minerals.
proposed_definition_plain: A mineral name officially accepted by the International Mineralogical Association, the international body that decides which minerals are recognized.
proposed_usageNote: Verify against the current IMA List of Minerals and record the list version or date consulted. If the CNMNC later discredits the name, re-type it as Obsolete.
proposed_scopeNote: Includes formally approved and grandfathered species names. Excludes names pending or lacking approval (Unapproved), discredited names (Obsolete), variety names (Variety), and group and series names, which are typed separately.
review_comment: Conceptually a specialization of Official Name (with the IMA as the authority); consider skos:broader Official Name rather than Authoritative Name. Overlaps Species for mineral names; clarify whether a name may carry more than one type.

skos:definition: The name of a mineralogical group a specimen belongs to. Groups are defined as part of authoritative classification systems as a mechanism to group a set of mineral species with essentially the same crystal structure and composed of chemically similar elements.
proposed_definition_concise: A name for a category above species rank in an authoritative classification that brings together related members.
proposed_definition_technical: A name designating a category at group rank (including supergroups and subgroups) within an authoritative classification system, comprising two or more species or subordinate categories that share the characteristics by which that system defines the group.
proposed_definition_plain: The name of a family of related minerals or meteorites that experts have grouped together, such as the feldspar group or the H chondrite group.
proposed_usageNote: Where the group is defined by shared crystal structure and chemistry (as in IMA-CNMNC mineral nomenclature), prefer the narrower Structural Group. Record the classification system from which the group name is taken.
proposed_scopeNote: Covers group-rank names in mineral, rock, and meteorite classifications, including supergroups and subgroups. Excludes species names (Species) and solid-solution series names (Series).
review_comment: Original definition is mineral-specific and duplicates Structural Group. Proposed text generalizes it so that meteorite groups (e.g., Weisberg, McCoy & Krot 2006) and other group-rank names are covered.

skos:definition: An alias of a mineral name used within a historical context or derived from a historical source
proposed_definition_concise: An alternate name for a geological material attested in historical sources or past usage.
proposed_definition_technical: An alternate name for a geological material documented in historical literature, labels, catalogs, or other archival sources, recorded for its historical or provenance value irrespective of its current nomenclatural status.
proposed_definition_plain: An older name found in old books, labels, or records, kept because it shows how the material was known in the past.
proposed_usageNote: Use to preserve names found on original labels, ledgers, or in historical literature; record the source and, where known, the date or period. If the principal reason for recording the name is that an authority has discredited or withdrawn it, use Obsolete instead.
proposed_scopeNote: Includes archaic, pre-standard, and vernacular names found in historical documents, for any geological material (not only minerals).
review_comment: Original definition is limited to mineral names, which is narrower than the parent Geological Material Name. Overlaps Obsolete and Synonym; the proposed distinction is basis (historical source/period) versus status (discredited).

skos:definition: An alias of a mineral species no longer recognized as the official classification
proposed_definition_concise: An alternate name that refers to the same material as a currently accepted name.
proposed_definition_technical: An alternate name that denotes the same material (e.g., the same mineral species) as a currently accepted authoritative name but is not itself the accepted name, including redundant names, spelling and transliteration variants, and names superseded by the accepted name.
proposed_definition_plain: Another name for the same mineral or material, used instead of or alongside its official name.
vann:usageNote: It is recommended to use synonyms only as additional information to the officially accepted IMA name.
proposed_usageNote: Record synonyms only as supplementary information alongside the accepted name (e.g., the IMA-approved name); do not use a synonym as the primary identification. Where possible, link the synonym to the accepted name it corresponds to.
proposed_scopeNote: Includes redundant names and spelling or transliteration variants that map to a single accepted material. Excludes names for a subset of a species distinguished by color or habit (Variety) and names discredited without a single accepted equivalent (Obsolete).
review_comment: Original definition ('no longer recognized as the official classification') describes obsolescence rather than synonymy and overlaps Obsolete. Proposed text defines synonymy by reference to an accepted name.

skos:definition: A name defined in prior standards or classification systems but has since been removed from those authoritative sources. Includes names designated by the International Mineralogical Association as discredited or obsolete.
proposed_definition_concise: A name that has been discredited or withdrawn from the authoritative nomenclature in which it was once recognized.
proposed_definition_technical: An alternate name previously recognized in a formal nomenclature or classification system that has since been discredited, rejected, or withdrawn by the responsible authority (e.g., mineral names discredited by the IMA-CNMNC), and is therefore no longer valid for current identification.
proposed_definition_plain: A name that experts once accepted but have since officially dropped.
proposed_usageNote: Record the authority and, where known, the decision reference and date of discreditation or withdrawal. If the obsolete name corresponds to a currently valid material, also record that material's accepted name.
proposed_scopeNote: Includes IMA-discredited mineral names and names withdrawn from rock and meteorite classifications. Excludes names that were never formally recognized (use Historical or Alternate Name).
review_comment: Minor grammar issue in original ('...classification systems but has since been removed' lacks a subject). Note that Alternate Name's original definition ('nor sanctioned by an authoritative body') technically excludes once-sanctioned names; see proposed wording on that row.

skos:definition: A mineral that is a type of the mineral species, distinguished by color or other optical phenomenon or characteristic
proposed_definition_concise: A name for a subset of a mineral species distinguished by color, habit, optical phenomenon, or trace-element content.
proposed_definition_technical: An alternate name for a recognized subset of a mineral species distinguished by a non-essential characteristic (such as color, habit, optical phenomenon, or trace-element content) without differing in the crystal structure or essential chemistry that define the species; variety names have no formal status in IMA-CNMNC nomenclature.
proposed_definition_plain: A special name for a particular form of a mineral that looks different, often because of its color, such as amethyst (purple quartz) or ruby (red corundum).
proposed_usageNote: Record the variety name together with the species to which it belongs (e.g., amethyst with quartz). Do not use a variety name in place of the species name for identification.
proposed_scopeNote: Includes gemological and mineralogical varieties of a single species. Excludes names of intermediate compositions within a solid-solution series (Series) and trade names spanning more than one species (Alternate Name).
review_comment: Original definition ('A mineral that is a type of...') defines a mineral rather than a name; the concept is a name type.

skos:definition: A name by which a geologic material is frequently referred, without reference to any formal usage or structure nor sanctioned by an authoritative body
proposed_definition_concise: A name for a geological material that is not currently sanctioned by an authoritative body.
proposed_definition_technical: A name by which a geological material is commonly known or referred to that is not currently assigned or sanctioned by an authoritative body under a formal nomenclature; the broader type for historical, synonymous, obsolete, varietal, and unapproved names.
proposed_definition_plain: Any other name people use for a material that is not its official name.
proposed_usageNote: Use directly for common, trade, local, or colloquial names that fit no narrower alternate-name type. Record alongside, not instead of, an authoritative name where one is known.
proposed_scopeNote: Includes common, trade, vernacular, varietal, historical, obsolete, and unapproved names. Excludes names assigned by an authority under a formal nomenclature (Authoritative Name) and curatorial names given to a collection object (Object Name).
review_comment: Original wording ('nor sanctioned by an authoritative body') excludes the narrower concept Obsolete, whose names were once sanctioned; proposed text says 'not currently sanctioned'.

skos:definition: The name of a mineralogical specimen that is pending approval as an offical name by the International Mineralogical Association (IMA)
proposed_definition_concise: A mineral name that has not received International Mineralogical Association (IMA-CNMNC) approval, including names proposed and awaiting a decision.
proposed_definition_technical: A name for a mineral or putative mineral that has not been approved by the IMA-CNMNC, whether because a proposal is pending decision, has not been submitted, or the name was published without approval; the name has no official standing unless and until it is approved.
proposed_definition_plain: A mineral name that has not (or not yet) been officially accepted by the International Mineralogical Association.
proposed_usageNote: Where a proposal is pending, record the IMA proposal number (of the form IMA YYYY-NNN) if known, and re-type the name as IMA Approved Name once approval is published.
proposed_scopeNote: Includes names under review, names published without CNMNC approval, and informal names for unnamed or insufficiently characterized minerals. Excludes names discredited after approval (Obsolete).
review_comment: Original definition covers only names pending approval; proposed text also covers names never submitted or published without approval. Decide which scope is intended. Typo in original: 'offical'.

skos:altLabel: Cataloged Name, Cataloged As, Specimen Name
skos:definition: The name of a collection object (compound specimen) for curatorial, cataloging, and/or presentation purposes.
proposed_definition_concise: A name given to a collection object as a whole for curatorial, cataloging, or display purposes.
proposed_definition_technical: A name assigned by a collection-holding institution to a collection object as a whole (typically a compound specimen comprising several materials) for cataloging, curation, or presentation, independent of the names of its constituent materials.
proposed_definition_plain: The name a museum gives a specimen as a whole in its catalog or on display, which may differ from the names of the minerals it contains.
vann:usageNote: Cataloged name is generally applied to a compound specimen where physical cataloging is based on the object rather than its constituent parts.
proposed_usageNote: Apply at the level of the whole object, particularly for compound specimens cataloged as a single object rather than by constituent parts. Record the names of individual constituent materials separately, using the appropriate name types.
proposed_scopeNote: Includes catalog names, display names, and specimen names for whole objects (e.g., 'Fluorite on Quartz'). Excludes names of individual constituent materials.
review_comment: altLabel 'Cataloged Name' duplicates the prefLabel of a separate concept, and 'Specimen Name' is described in Verbatim Name's usage note as an alternate label for that concept. Merge Object Name and Cataloged Name (or make Cataloged Name narrower of Object Name) and assign each label to one concept only.

skos:definition: A name assigned by an authoritative body based on a defined set of unambiguous criteria and belonging to a formal nomenclature
proposed_definition_concise: A name constructed according to the rules of a formal nomenclature.
proposed_definition_technical: A name constructed in accordance with the rules of a published formal nomenclature or classification scheme (e.g., IUGS igneous rock nomenclature with prescribed mineral qualifiers), whether or not that specific name has been individually assigned or registered by an authority.
proposed_definition_plain: A name built by following an official naming rulebook, even if no committee approved that exact name.
proposed_usageNote: Use for rule-derived compound or qualified names that follow a formal scheme but are not themselves entries in an authority's register. For names individually assigned by an authority, use Authoritative Name or its narrower types.
proposed_scopeNote: Includes rule-derived names built within a formal scheme, such as IUGS igneous rock names with mineral qualifiers. Excludes informal, trade, and curatorial names.
review_comment: Original definition is identical to Authoritative Name's, and 'Formal Name' is also an altLabel of Authoritative Name. Either deprecate this concept (owl:deprecated true; dct:isReplacedBy Authoritative Name) or adopt the proposed distinction (rule-conforming vs. authority-assigned) and remove the altLabel from Authoritative Name.

skos:altLabel: The name under which a compound specimen is recorded in a collection catalog.
skos:definition: Cataloged name is generally applied to a compound specimen where physical cataloging is based on the object rather than its constituent parts.
proposed_definition_concise: The name under which a compound specimen is recorded in a collection catalog.
proposed_definition_technical: A name recorded in a collection catalog for a compound specimen as a whole, identifying the specimen by its principal (parent) material where physical cataloging is based on the object rather than on its constituent parts.
proposed_definition_plain: The name used in the museum catalog for a specimen made of several minerals, usually named after the main one.
proposed_usageNote: Use when the catalog record names the object by its principal material (e.g., a specimen cataloged as 'Fluorite' that also carries quartz). Record the other constituent materials with their own name types.
skos:scopeNote: Tightly scoped to compound specimens (the parent material in a compound specimen)
proposed_scopeNote: Restricted to compound specimens; applies to the name of the parent or principal material under which the whole specimen is cataloged. Not used for single-material specimens or for names of constituent parts.
review_comment: Original definition reads as a usage note rather than a definition, and repeats Object Name's usage note. Overlaps Object Name (which lists 'Cataloged Name' as an altLabel); recommend merging or setting skos:broader Object Name.

skos:definition: The unstructured name of a geological material for general, storage, curatorial, and/or presentation purposes.
proposed_definition_concise: The name of a geological material as originally recorded, without interpretation or standardization.
proposed_definition_technical: A name for a geological material recorded exactly as it appears in the original source (label, ledger, field notes, or legacy database) as unparsed free text, prior to any interpretation, correction, or mapping to a controlled nomenclature; analogous to the verbatim terms of Darwin Core.
proposed_definition_plain: The name exactly as written on the original label or record, copied without corrections.
vann:usageNote: For compound specimens, recommendation is to reserve this term for the specimen level and reserve alternate name for specimen parts. Specimen name is a common alternate label for verbatim names assigned at the compound specimen level.
proposed_usageNote: Transcribe the text exactly as found, including spelling errors, abbreviations, and punctuation, and pair it with an interpreted name of the appropriate type. For compound specimens, apply at the whole-specimen level and use Alternate Name (or a relevant narrower type) for names of specimen parts.
proposed_scopeNote: Includes transcribed label names, legacy catalog entries, and field names. Excludes names that have been normalized or interpreted against a controlled nomenclature.
review_comment: Original definition ('for general, storage, curatorial, and/or presentation purposes') overlaps Object Name; proposed text aligns with the Darwin Core sense of 'verbatim' (as recorded). Original usage note's mention of 'Specimen name' as an alternate label conflicts with Object Name's altLabel 'Specimen Name'.

skos:definition: A name derived from an authoritative classification system at the rank of species
proposed_definition_concise: An authoritative name for a category at species rank in a formal classification.
proposed_definition_technical: An authoritative name designating a category at species rank within a formal classification system; for minerals, a species defined by a unique combination of chemical composition and crystal structure as recognized by the IMA-CNMNC.
proposed_definition_plain: The official name of one specific kind of mineral, such as quartz or calcite.
proposed_usageNote: Use for the name of the species to which a specimen has been identified. For minerals, check the name against the IMA List of Minerals.
proposed_scopeNote: Restricted to species rank. Excludes group, series, and variety names.
review_comment: Label clash with the altLabel 'Species' on the broader concept Classification. Overlaps IMA Approved Name for mineral names; clarify whether a name may carry both types, or whether IMA Approved Name should be narrower of Species.

skos:definition: A name that has been formally approved and entered into a register of record by the designated authority holding jurisdiction over nomenclature in that entity's domain, following the authority's published criteria, and that remains subject to continuing review and possible revision by that authority.
proposed_definition_concise: A name formally approved and registered by the authority with jurisdiction over nomenclature in its domain.
proposed_definition_technical: A name that has been formally approved and entered in a register of record by the authority holding jurisdiction over nomenclature in its domain, in accordance with that authority's published criteria, and that remains subject to the authority's continuing review and possible revision.
proposed_definition_plain: A name that the responsible official body has approved and entered in its official list.
vann:usageNote: Examples of authorities in the geological collections domain includes the IMA (mineral names) and the Meteoritical Society (meteorite names)
proposed_usageNote: Record the authority and the register consulted, with the date consulted, since official status may change. Examples: the IMA List of Minerals for mineral names; the Meteoritical Bulletin Database for meteorite names.
proposed_scopeNote: Includes officially approved mineral names and officially approved names of individual meteorites. Excludes names that follow a formal scheme but are not individually registered (Formal Name) and names awaiting approval (Unapproved).
review_comment: Also listed as an altLabel of its broader concept Authoritative Name; remove that altLabel. Consider making IMA Approved Name narrower of Official Name. Grammar in original usage note ('Examples ... includes').
